utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody in and around the courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-81-T, The Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have appearances for today, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours, counsel. My name is Mark Harmon. Appearing today for the Prosecution is Ann Sutherland, and Carmela Javier is assisting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everybody in the process. Defence of General Perisic will be represented today by our assistants Mr. Androvic, case manager Tasic, and Novak Lukic as Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Lukic. Good morning, Mr. Tesic. Mr. Tesic, just again to repeat the usual warning that you are still bound by the declaration you made at the beginning of your testimony to tell the truth, the whole truth and nothing else but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Madam Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, towards the end of yesterday's session we were looking at a document relating to the pullout of the troops from Bosnia-Herzegovina. If we could have Rule 65 ter number -- sorry, Exhibit P368 on the screen, please. At LiveNote transcript page 66, you were shown a copy of a document contained within that exhibit, and that's Bosnia -- B/C/S, page 2; in English, page 3. And you were asked who the document was from, and you said that it could be from the commander of the Special Units Corps but that you couldn't see that on the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honours, we took the original from the vault last night and had it rescanned into the computer. I have a hard copy here. If it could be given to the witness and Mr. Lukic -- shown to Mr. Lukic before it's given to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sutherland, I'm advised that this be exhibit was under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We should be in closed session, maybe, when you use it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into closed session. 2 [Closed session] [Confidentiality lifted by order of Trial Chamber I]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just see that on e-court there is another document other than the one shown to Mr. Tesic, so it could have been mistakenly retrieved or could be mistakenly marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that a correct one now, Mr. Lukic? Thank you very much. How do you see that when it is so illegible? You don't have to answer that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honours, the English translation that's on the screen is the unrevised translation. We are in the process of having it revised, but the witness has the document in front of him, and he can read the specific paragraph that I want to take him to, so that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do that -- going to the witness, ma'am, if it is an unrevised version, I guess we agreed that in such a situation then we mark for identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It was our understanding that if the Defence objected to an unrevised translation, then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Were they aware that it was unrevised?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: They were?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Were you aware, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, it has the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me ask Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We would have to be aware of that, but if you allow me, during the break we are going to check whether anything contingent is contained in this translation, and then later on we will let you know whether we stipulate that it be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is already admitted, Mr. Lukic. You didn't object. I want to know whether at the time when it was admitted, were you aware that it is a draft version?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot state so clearly. What I see in front of me does not bear the marking "unrevised" or "draft translation."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Anyway, it's admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I presume that there's nothing contentious there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just add that earlier in -- during an earlier witness's evidence, I told the Court and the Defence that if the ERN starts with the number starts with the letters "ET," then that is a DVU translation, can we say, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What is a DVU, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It's the document video unit or whatever within the OTP, and actually, in the footer of this document it does have OTP-DVU.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which means?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Which means that it's not the CLSS translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, DVU we are hearing for the first time today, so we will learn as we go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, looking at that document now, can you tell who the document is from?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Perhaps if we could go down to the bottom of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I guess there's nothing for us to see on the screen? The document that is being seen is the one which is in the hands of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. Because the document has been admitted, our case manager is unable to upload exhibits, and so I have to refer to it by doc ID 0633-1148.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is there anything specific we are waiting for?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The document to come up on e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Oh.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So this is the rescanned -- this is the one that's been taken --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is the copy. The B/C/S copy is the one that's been copied from the original from the vault last evening.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, are you able to see now who the document from?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And who is that?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Document of the command of Special Units Corps of the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You also said yesterday that the person who approved the pullout of the troops was contained in paragraph 1 of that document. As we don't have an English -- revised English translation, are you able to read paragraph 1 into the record?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "Because of the apparent need and following approval of the General staff of the Yugoslavia army, prepare the unit to pull out from the area of Vogosca."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, can you see before the words -- before the acronym GYVJ, do you see a letter "N"?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And what does that stand for?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And so if that sentence is read again, could you read the beginning of that sentence again up until the end of the words "VJ"?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The chief of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia..."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to turn now – I’ve finished with that document. I want to turn now to discuss the issue of logbooks. Was it protocol for all units to keep correspondence logbooks?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: War diary had to be kept by units at the rank of battalion and above.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I guess, Madam Sutherland, that there is no further need for us to be in closed session.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I was just about to request that we go back into open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Madam Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Tesic, my question was in relation to logbooks, correspondence logbooks in particular. Was it protocol for all units to keep a correspondence logbook?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Record books are maintained at the level of brigades and higher commands and institutions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Within the correspondence logbooks, do they include oral orders?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could we have Rule 65 ter number 08780 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What is it? 087?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: 80. 08780. Your Honours, we have the --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: First of all, Mr. Tesic, can you see what this document is?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a register of the Special Units Corps of the army of Yugoslavia started in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, we only have certain extracts of the logbook translated, and I will take the witness to two in particular. This is an extract of a document that we received, which only has extracts from the 21st of December, 1993, until the 31st of December, 1993. If we could now go to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are these documents the same document? I mean, it doesn't look like the left looks like the right side.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. That's because the front page hasn't been translated. If we could go to entry number 4566, which is in the B/C/S, page 4, and the English, page 2, and it may actually be easier for the witness to read, I have a hard copy of the B/C/S. If this could be handed to the witness and shown to the Defence beforehand.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, the copy that I've given you runs chronologically. Unfortunately, the copy that's in e-court has been scanned in not chronologically. So the page for you would be 7, page 7 of that document you have in front of you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So for us to be able to follow the B/C/S version, could my learned friend please tell us which item number, and could you enlarge the B/C/S, that part where the witness is going to testify about for the benefit of Mr. Perisic because he can't see properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 4566, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And it's on page 4 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And we would also appreciate an enlargement of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, if we can go from left to right --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed, madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, if we can take the document, and looking at the columns from left to right, can you explain to the Court what column 3 means?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Column number 3 refers to the level of confidentiality of a document. It is indicated here "DT," which stands for "state secret," "drzavna tajna," "state secret."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, the date of the document?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date of the document is the 30th of December, 1993, since this logbook is from 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What does -- and then the next column is -- what does that relate to, column number 5?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Column number 5 indicates the command or institution or the first and last name of the person. It is Military Post 1410 Nis.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry. If we can go to column number 5 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, the name of the last person, it is something, something, Nis. I don't understand what that -- I didn't understand the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was Military Postbox 1410 Nis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Right, but I guess we've got to know whether the name of this person is the sender or the recipient. I think top of the heading there says "sender." Is this the name of the person who is sending the document, or is it the name of the person who is going to receive the document?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. If I may, the witness is actually looking at the first entry on that page, which is entry number 4564.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, aren't we looking at entry number 4566?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: That's what I was just about to take the witness to.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Witness, can you go back across -- looking at entry number 4566.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It has in column 3 the words "DT," which you've explained means state secret. It then has in column 4 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The date, which is explained.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The date, which is in -- which is following the date up on -- of the first entry. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And then in the third column for entry number 4566, does it have the same quotation marks that it's following the entry of the entry above?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And so if we look at entry 4565, the one directly above the one that I'm interested in, we see the words "SP." What does that relate to in relation to column 5?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I presume that's an acronym for "own needs."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So if we go back to column 4, that's the date of registration, not the date of the document; is that correct? The date that it's put into the register?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So then if we go to column number 6, in fact, that's the date of the document, is it not? But in this case, there is no date there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: However, we can see from entry at the top of the page, which is entry number 4564, that the date is the -- is it correct, the 29th of December, 29.12?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are coming back to the questions from yesterday. It would be fair for the witness to be asked question, on the basis of what he can see, when does he think the document was drafted?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I take my learned colleague's point.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, looking at this document, looking at this page, can you tell me the date that you -- the date of the document 4566 came into being?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Was he the author of that document?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How he is going to know when the date is not mentioned in the document? Are you inviting speculation?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, point taken. Point taken, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So looking at entry number 4566, if we go to column number 7, what does it say there?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It explains a brief content of the document and in this case, assistance to army of RS, Republika Srpska, in execution of their operations. It addressed to the Guards Motorised Brigade, so being the organisational unit indicated.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And then finally, the columns number 9 and 10, what does -- what do they relate to?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under 9, date refers most probably to the date of delivery or receipt; and column 10, that it is to be registered in the plan of use on a specified date, in this case 30th of 10, 1998, I presume. This is neither my signature nor my initials, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, I think yesterday you testified that you received an oral order two days before you went on the march; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And you said that you wouldn't have gone on the march without a written order; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If -- could you please give us a reference of the witness's words? I'm not sure whether he has been quoted correctly. Let us take a look at what he really said.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: One moment. Page 6 of yesterday's LiveNote transcript. The witness answered: "I suppose --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: At what line, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry, line 6 to 9. On page 5, line 18, I asked at line 17: "How did you receive that order? Was it written or oral?" And the witness answered on 18: "Oral." And then over the page on page 6, when asking about the units engaged, I said: "Can you be more specific in relation to the units?" And the witness answered: "I suppose there is a written document governing the move of the units towards Vogosca. I don't have that document here with me, and I haven't seen it, but it's certain that regardless of the oral order, we would not have gone there without a written order."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that's what was said or read here is different from the mode in which the question was asked on line 12, row 3.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Page 12, line 3. Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My interpretation of yesterday's transcript as you read it, Madam Sutherland, is that the witness never saw a written order on the day he marched, but he marched on the basis of an oral order assuming that a written order exists somewhere. Now, the fact of the matter is, he didn't see it before he marched, or he marched on the basis of an oral order.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, in relation to entry number 4566, is this -- this is a document that's going to the Guards Brigade in relation to the assistance to the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you turn to entry number 4582, which is on page 9 for you, and in e-court it is on page 1, and the B/C/S, page 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sutherland, the Registry has a technical difficulty with the B/C/S side of it. Are you prepared and is the Defence agreeable to proceed with the English version only?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I have another copy here I can provide to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you could, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: There it comes now.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, in relation to entry number 4582, again, what is this entry?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a strictly confidential document addressed to the Guards Brigade. The date and number are clear. It's the 31st of December, and this is a document regulating the sortee of units into the field addressed to the chief of staff and operation centre. Also, the document is kept -- the next words are illegible. This is not my signature, but there is a reference to Vrana in the plan of use and number such and such, state secret.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Your Honour, I would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just get clarity. Am I right to be reading the distribution date to be the 11th of February, 1996? Yes, Mr. Tesic, would you like to comment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I have no comment, and the date is correct as you put it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 11th of February, 1996?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's what it says. I have no comment.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, in relation to these logbooks, you are familiar with the registers, are you not?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the extent that my previous job enabled me to learn about it, I am partially familiar with it. This is a document of the kind kept by the general affairs unit in the staff of the command, and an NCO is constantly working on this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What is an NCO?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Non --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Witness, Mr. Tesic, can you tell the Chamber what an NCO is?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: It's non-commissioned officer. In Serbian, "podificir." The witness does not understand the English acronym, so he is confused. He says:

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't find this abbreviation or acronym here. I don't know what you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think, Your Honour, President Moloto, you asked about the English acronym. He said that an NCO is working on this document, which is the English translation for the Serbian word, literally meaning "under officer." In Serbian, he said that an under officer is working normally on such a document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have the English version enlarged, please. I would like to be able to read what's written on column 10. Are we able to -- can we be told what is written on column 10?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I thought the witness had read out into the record, maybe on page 14 in the transcript by now.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: But, Mr. Tesic, can you read column 10 again for the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not very legible, but I'll do my best. It says: "... kept within the study 'Vrana' in the plan of use under number DT" -- meaning state secret -- "150-1 as of 30th October, 199" -- I think the last digit is 8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, the Presiding Judge had a question about the date of the document being 11th of February, 1996. Is that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The date of the distribution of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The date of the distribution in column 9. Is that -- what does that date relate to?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the date of distribution of the document, meaning that if somebody was issued with this document, this document was discharged, and we see who actually took it in column 10.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And so if that were right, that would mean that these documents, as we can see on this page, are being distributed two or three years after the event; is that correct or possible?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I suppose it's possible as long as it's written here with these dates.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender that document. The log itself --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- is 9 pages in total, and we would seek to have the entire excerpts in even though I have only taken the witness at this point to two of the entries.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And what would be the purpose of the remaining seven pages?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Because we would be intending to show it to witnesses in the future, Your Honour, or we can simply mark for identification -- admit the two entries that we looked at this morning and then leave the others for when the further witnesses come. It's a 9-page document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you were rising onto your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I think we should proceed as we did before. If two pages were shown to the witness, then two pages should be admitted now, and then if through some other witness more pages are introduced, then more pages should be introduced through another witness like we did with the transcripts from assembly sessions. I don't see why the whole document should be admitted if only two pages were shown to the witness. I think that is actually in keeping with your own rules.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, we agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Then the two pages -- it's page 1 and 2 in the English; I don't know what they are in the B/C/S, but the equivalent are admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Those pages will be Exhibit P369, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, what do you -- I now wish to turn to another topic. What do you understand the term "active defence" to mean?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In keeping with the orders received, active defence means keeping the position you are on ahead of the forward line and, as required, destroying targets that may emerge and responding to fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, when you were in Bosnia at the end of December 1993 and January 1994, did you have snipers in your unit?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Did your unit provide training to VRS snipers?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. I'm trying to remember. I think we assisted in the training and operation of the sniper rifles.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: How many units were involved? How many VRS units were involved?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are talking about individuals from a brigade. We didn't train units, but individuals.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: How many people?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say because that was not my job. It was not my responsibility, that training.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, may we go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into closed session. 7 [Closed session] [Confidentiality lifted by order of Trial Chamber I]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could have Exhibit number P353 on the screen, please, and if we could go to B/C/S, page 11, and the English, page 12.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, is this an entry that was written by you? It's --

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we can in fact just go to the previous page of the English, which will have date, and also the previous page of the B/C/S. I'm sorry. So we can see this is an entry for the 15th of January, 1994, and then going over to the following page, at the bottom of that entry for that date, we can see "Tasks."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: May we go to the following page, please, of both documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, what is the acronym -- under "Tasks," you see the acronym "VV-PPN" right at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What does that acronym stand for?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Military police platoon for special purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you direct us to the English part of it, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It's on the bottom of the screen, Your Honour, to that entry. There.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Under "Tasks," and there's the acronym VV-PPN.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, it says in the English translation: "Three officers of the military police special purposes" - what you've just said - "shall enter formation of Rajlovac brigade between 5 and 17 January, and two officers shall enter the formation of the Ilidza brigade between the 15th of January and the 17th of January to train the snipers of that brigade." Are you aware of how many -- how many people the two officers trained?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have that information.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Did you receive any reports back about the training?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was something that the commander of the brigades involved, the Rajlovac and the other brigade would receive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you aware of the size of those brigades?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And both the -- who did the Rajlovac and the Ilidza brigades belong to?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Sarajevo-Romanija Corps of the VRS, the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could go to entry number 20, which is in the B/C/S on page 9 and the English, page 10.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, this is an entry from the 11th of January, 1994. And I think this is an entry -- you didn't make this entry, did you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And it speaks there about: "... offensive operations shall be continued along all directions." Which direction -- can you describe for the Court the directions that are referred to that you're aware of where offensive operations were being conducted?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here, the main axis of attack shall be Rajlovac, Sokolje, Svabino hill.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And then we see another reference to engaging staff sergeant Dukic in the training of snipers for the needs of the Ilidza Brigade?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's written there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. Just one moment, Your Honour. I have no further questions for the witness. Thank you, Mr. Tesic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Bear with me for a moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And Your Honour, we're still in closed session. I don't know whether Mr. Lukic wishes to be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, I don't think so. May we please move into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And before we begin, may I ask if I could have that document, the logbook document back, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Tesic. My name is Novak Lukic. On behalf of the Defence team for Mr. Perisic, I will be asking you a few questions. Before we start, I'd like to ask you, since we are speaking the same language, to wait a second or two before you start answering so that the interpreters could keep up and the transcript would reflect everything correctly. My first question has to do with your prior statements. Is it true that to date you have given only one statement to the Prosecution; your only interview with the Prosecution was in 2003?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, and representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor attended.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From 2003 onwards and before you came to The Hague, did you receive calls from the OTP, and did you give them any new statements?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you asked in the past five years to give any new statements by the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As you told us at the beginning of your evidence, until a few months ago, you occupied a very high position in the Ministry of the Interior, you were commander of the Gendarmes, and you were retired this last summer?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In fact, you were man number 3 in the Serbian police all these years?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no such rating, but that would be approximately true.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to ask you a few questions about the Guards Brigade. On the first day of your testimony - that was last Thursday - the page of the transcript is 1888, line 22, in response to a question from the Prosecution, you said that before the enactment of the law on the VJ, the Guards Brigade was subordinated to the Ministry of Defence. That's what you said, and I would like us to be a bit more precise. Did you mean the Federal Secretariat for National Defence?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In 1991, 1992, it was called the Federal Secretariat for National Defence, the Office of the Federal Secretary, General Kadijevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's right. And the Guards Brigade until the enactment of the Law on the Army and the Establishment of the Ministry of Defence and the General Staff was subordinated to the Federal Secretariat of National Defence and only then after the enactment of that law became subordinate to the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your statement to the Prosecution, paragraph 7 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Madam Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry for interrupting, but can there be more of a pause between the questions and answers because it's very confusing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree. I do have that problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just so that we are clear, and I see some years here, 1991 and 1992, can we be told when this Law on the Army and Establishment of the Ministry of Defence was enacted so that we know exactly what time we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the year, Mr. Tesic, when the Law on the Army was enacted, when it came into force?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us put on the screen your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's 1D00-1776, B/C/S, page 3, and English, page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In that statement to the OTP, you said sometime in 1997 the Guards Brigade became directly subordinated -- that's paragraph 7. We need to zoom in on the B/C/S a bit. It says: "In 1997, when Milosevic became the president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, the Guards Brigade became directly subordinated to the president of the FRY." Do you remember stating that to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me read it please. Where is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we zoom in on paragraph 7 in B/C/S for the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My information is that it was in the beginning of 1998, but that is not so important to me. My question is, do you remember that just after the Guards Brigade became directly subordinated to the president of the FRY, General Perisic was soon replaced from his position as Chief of General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia? It was a very publicized affair.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure, but I think I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To be quite precise, in my previous question when I said that after the enactment of the Law on the Army, the Guards Brigade became subordinated to the General Staff; it was in fact part of the newly established Special Units Corps and through the Special Units Corps was subordinated to the General Staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would I be right in saying that the main function of the Guards Brigade was in fact to provide security to the highest political and military leaders in peacetime and in wartime provide security to the highest command, to the Supreme Command?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stated earlier that -- its three main tasks in peacetime: One, training; two, securing combat readiness; and three, protocol duties, that means security for installations, residencies, et cetera. And in wartime, the Guards Brigade was to secure the Supreme Command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I interrupt, Mr. Lukic. At line 12 of page 24 up to line 16, you refer in a question to the fact that the Guards Brigade was part of the newly established Special Units Corps, and you've been talking here so far, at the previous question, you were referring to the year 1998. Can we establish what we mean by newly established? When was it established because I think the Special Units Corps we heard about being mentioned.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for His Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To dispel any doubts, Mr. Tesic, do you know when approximately the Special Units Corps was established?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think sometime in 1993, mid-1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I presume that this is clear now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When we talk about the basic function of the Guards Brigade, would you agree with me that primarily its function was not to engage in combat activities. It's primary function is providing security; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And in fact, first contact with what Guards Brigade was not meant to do was the engagement in the Vukovar operation in 1991 when it took active part in combat operations?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I fully agree with your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Contrary to what we have been hearing in your testimony in the past couple of days, there is a huge difference in the participation of the Guards Brigade in the Vukovar events in 1991 and the participation of parts of the guards unit in 1993 and 1994 in the Sarajevo theatre of war because back then in 1991 in Vukovar, the whole Guards Brigade went to the frontline except for some staff units, smaller staff units. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know how many, approximately, men did the Guards Brigade have in 1991 and then in 199 -- and was there any difference in the number of troops and officers in 1993 in December from that previous figure?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have specific data, but I believe there were more than 3.000 members in Vukovar in 1991, and in 1993 there were -- approximately together with command and all the units, there were 1.600, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you were part of the Special Units Corps?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, and that is the thesis of the -- this Tribunal in another case, that the Guards Brigade were the creme de la creme, the most elite unit of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you given the criteria for the selection of both officers, non-commissioned officers, and troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Specificity of the Guards Brigade was also that it was the only brigade to have two battalions of military police within its ranks. In its infantry -- in a typical infantry brigade, military police would be a company strength unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Guards Brigade had two military police battalion but only for a period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In 1993 in December, do you remember the composition of military police within the brigade?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1993, there was a battalion of military police within the ranks of the Guards Brigade, and it had one company in APCs, armoured personnel vehicles, and two police companies.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And that was another thing that they were specific about, and that is anti-sabotage or anti-terrorist unit. First, it was a platoon for special purposes, but it was a specialised unit within the ranks of the whole of JNA, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a military police for special purposes platoon. It is 30 strong. For awhile, it was autonomous, and for awhile it was part of the military police battalion of the Guards Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, as per establishment, what is the number of men in an infantry brigade, or generally? Is there any difference between the infantry and motorised brigade, so the number and the composition of a brigade? Could you expand on that, please.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Motorised brigades out of all the brigades in the VJ was the most numerous. In peacetime, it would number some 2 to 3.000 troops, and in wartime between 3 and a half and 4.000.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what about infantry brigades?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slightly less but approximately the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You must know that the VRS adapted its structure or copied its structure from JNA regulations governing the composition of -- and structure of its military units, those regulations dating before 1991?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I presume, but I never analysed this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's start discussing the events from 1993 and the structure of the Guards Brigade in 1993 and 1994. Yesterday in your testimony, you mentioned something which I'd like you to explain to the Bench. At that time, there were two categories of soldiers at that time, regular soldier and contract soldiers. First of all, please provide an explanation about the contract soldiers.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Contract soldiers are persons who had done their military service and who signed a certain contract for a certain period of time on employment with a certain military postbox.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So in a way, professional soldiers because they received salaries -- well, regular soldiers used to receive some remuneration, but the salary of those contract soldiers was closer to regular monthly salary outside the military, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Contract soldiers are permanently employed in -- for the period stated in the contract, and they receive salaries and all the benefits as if they were fully employed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As fully employed as elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is exactly what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In that period towards the end of 1993, you were Chief of -- could you tell us the exact function that you occupied, the post?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1993, I was -- in 1993, I was operations officer in the operations organ of the staff of the Guards Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have information that in the group that departed on the 30th of December or towards the end of December - but I believe it was the 30th - for the Sarajevo theatre of war that exclusively officers, non-commissioned officers and contract soldiers numbered in that group, so could you confirm that being the operations officer in the operations organ of that brigade? Could you concur with me?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, your information is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So on that occasion, no regular soldiers were part of that group, regular soldiers being those who finished their national service and training but had not entered into a contract with the military, so they had not entered the military.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not have such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you a couple of questions concerning the first group, and when I say the first group, I mean those who departed in mid-December; most of them came from the 72nd Special Brigade. Do you know, on the basis of what I have access to, Colonel Stupar was heading that group, and at that time he was a commander of the 72nd Special Brigade? Do you remember? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard that in mid-December they departed and the commander was with them, the commander of the 72nd Brigade, then Lieutenant-Colonel, then later Colonel Stupar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You also testified that in the first group there were some officers and I presume soldiers who had contracts from the Guards Motorised Brigade. Do you know anything about how this first group was structured? What was the basis for the selection of the personnel? Do you know anything about how it was organised, the first group?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not have such information. It is up to commander of the battalion, 2nd Motorised Battalion, Major Borovcanin who was engaged in that task.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You found him there in Vogosca when you came to that place?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He came to Park Hotel in Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And last question before the break. Do you know that Mr. Borovcanin was born in the area of Romanija, which is very close to Vogosca in Bosnia Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Lieutenant-Colonel Borovcanin was born in the surrounds of Sokolac in the area of Romanija, Republika Srpska in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, now we can take a break if you so please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll take a break and come back at quarter to 11.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked you before the break about Mr. Borovcanin, and you provided an answer. I think you said earlier, not during your testimony but during your proofing that also saw Major Kosoric [Realtime transcript read in error, "Kosevic"] from the tank unit. My question is, is it known to you where he hales from?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Major Kosoric, I think he was born in Han Pijesak or the surrounds of Han Pijesak, Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This did not enter the record. I asked you about Major Kosoric, didn't I?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Major Kosoric. It says Major Kosevic here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Those mistakes will be rectified later on. He was also a member of the Special Units Corps. I presume he was in the armoured brigade. He wasn't part of the Guards Brigade, or was he?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Major Kosoric worked in the armoured brigade, and later on he was in the command of the Special Units Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's briefly address another topic. May I ask the testimony -- statement given to the OTP, 1D00-1776, Serbian, page 16, English, page 18, paragraph 77. The Prosecutor during the interview in 2003 asked you about officers and at paragraph -- explains that. He asked you about officers who went to the VRS from within the VJ unit. Pertaining to the personnel centre, I'm going to read out parts of your statement and ask you whether you still stand by it today.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you could zoom in on paragraph 77 in the B/C/S, please. Your Honours, this is not a topic which follows from examination-in-chief, but as per your guidelines I do believe it is relevant for this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "In November 1992, the service of VJ members in the VRS was not regulated, for instance, compensation. Later, I do not remember exactly when, the 30th Personnel Centre was established, the personnel centre, acronym KC. I heard from other officers that talks were conducted with them in the 30th KC about their readiness to serve in the VRS. I was also told that the 30th KC also took part in sending people over the border and that they were told that it would all be legal. They were mainly officers born in BiH or whose families lived in those parts. I can speak only about those I know. These officers also told me that there were no pressures exerted on them to go and serve in the VRS." My brief question, Mr. Tesic, concerning this is as follows: In what you said in this paragraph to the OTP, you said that based on what you heard from the officers who through the services of the 30th KC became officers of the VRS; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And those you spoke to told you that there was no pressure exerted on them to go to serve in the VRS; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you stand by what you said in your statement without any additions or alterations; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stand by it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may, just for clarity. I see the statement says that these officers were mainly born in the BiH. Were there any who were not born in the BiH? I'm asking you, Mr. Tesic. Were there any members of the personnel centre who were not born in the BiH who served in the VRS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have such information. I have no information of anybody working in the VRS haling from the territory of Republic of Serbia or from any other location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The only reason I'm asking the question is because the statement says they were mainly officers born in the BiH, suggesting that the majority were born in the BiH but that some may have been born elsewhere. That's the only reason I'm asking you. Are you able to explain why you use the word "mainly"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is because I'm not certain. I did not have the information. I could not access their personnel files or any lists so that I could be 100 percent sure that this is so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But those you knew to belong to the 30th Personnel Centre according to your knowledge were born in the BiH?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll now move on to the topic that interests us the most, namely, your departure and your stay in the Vogosca area. What was not quite clear to me from the transcript is what information you had about this. The eight members of the 72nd Special Brigade who were killed, their bodies remained in the territory controlled by the BH Army, correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: They got killed in combat on the 27th of December, 1993, and their bodies could not be recovered at the time?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, in the examination-in-chief, page 1929, line 2, you said when the last body of a killed member of the 72nd Brigade was turned over to your forces by the BH Army, which was either on the 25th or the 28th of January, you returned immediately thereafter?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our return started ...

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: May I just interrupt. Mr. Lukic, I'm sorry. Do you have a LiveNote page for that? I know you've given the transcript page, but unfortunately, the transcript wasn't available to us this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation] Lines 9 to 11 on page 51, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me, Mr. Tesic -- you spoke yesterday about the mission of your group when you went to that area. Do you agree with me that your primary task of the unit was to go there and secure the location so you could recover the bodies of the dead members of the 72nd Brigade?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that our task was to recover the bodies of the members of the 72nd Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You had to occupy certain positions held previously by the 72nd Brigade group that had withdrawn before your arrival, that is, to keep the frontline?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and this handover/takeover was completed on the 5th of January, 1994. The replacement, the rotation of units was the responsibility of Lieutenant-Colonel Vukasinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You answered a question from the Prosecution today as to the definition of active defence. Based on your recollection and all the documents you had the occasion to see over the past few days, would you agree that when your unit was there in that area, you did not participate much in active activities or action; you were mainly holding the line?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said during proofing to the Prosecution that we did not move an inch forward during our entire stay there, and I stand by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You told that to the Prosecution during your two-day proofing, correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at 65 ter 9069, page 1 in B/C/S --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do that, Mr. Lukic, what would you like to do with ID 001776, the witness's statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not tendering it. I think this is a public document, isn't it? Could the Prosecution confirm? The document I called up a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It's protected. Sorry, I was looking at your list.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we then remove it from the screen until we find out.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to my information, it's not protected, so can we call up this document again.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm terribly sorry. My records show that it is protected for the time being.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please remove it from the screen quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we then move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session. 3 [Private session] [Confidentiality lifted by order of Trial Chamber I]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This document you will see now on the screen, I suppose it's one of those shown to you by the Prosecution during proofing. And before we get it, I'd like to ask you, do you remember that at that time in your unit there was a problem getting salaries, and getting salaries was very important at the time because of the runaway hyper-inflation, and you needed your families to get the money?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll get the document on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is a letter from the commander of the Special Units Corps, Mr. Panic, from Vogosca sent to his chief of the financial services of the 7th of January, 1994. We have already heard evidence that on the 24th of January the dinar currency changed, and there was a galloping hyper-inflation. It was important to you, wasn't it, that you and your families in Belgrade get that money as quickly as possible?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was certainly very important because our families could not survive the next 24 hours if they had nothing to live on. If you didn't get your salary today, the next day for the same money you could only buy a piece of bread for your entire salary.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My learned friend asked you yesterday several questions about the rotation of personnel and you explained, if I understood correctly, that a smaller group would go to Belgrade to run some personal errands and then come back shortly. Do you remember if this was one of the reasons why people had to go to Belgrade, that is to solve their financial problems and get the money to their families?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't answer this question. I don't know why they went to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You told the Prosecutor earlier today that you got the orders to go on this assignment two days prior to your departure, which mean that if you went on the 30th, you learned about it two days before?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can I conclude from these problems with your per diem and your salaries that you did not reckon you would be staying in that area for a long time?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D17, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The answer of the witness is not recorded -- yes, it has been recorded. The question I asked on page 37, line 12, the witness answered yes. I believe this document should be under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Will it please be kept under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now move to private session -- back to open session, sorry, for awhile.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, I'd like now to move to a different subject; that is the relationship of subordination. The principle of every army is the principle of single command, that there is a subordinate superior relationship and a chain of command, correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When I asked you about the involvement of the Guards Brigade in the Vukovar operation, do you agree with me that the Guards Brigade, which at the time was subordinated directly to the Federal Secretary for National Defence, was resubordinated to the first army when they went to Vukovar, and they received orders from the commander of the first army, correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would object to this line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Why, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The relevance to this indictment. This is events in Vukovar in 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm asking this question, Your Honour, because I want to show how the chain of command functions in combat operations. It's the chain of command, and that's why I am comparing the Vukovar situation when the Guards Brigade followed one chain of command and the Romanija situation when they followed a different chain of command. I'm showing how a unit operates in different combat operations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The question is allowed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Whether the Guards Brigade was fully resubordinated to the first army, I don't know, but for the rest I agree with you completely.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I mean the part of the Guards Brigade that was actively involved in the operations group south, when they joined the operations group south, they became subordinated to the first military district and received orders from Commander Panic?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that a large number of documents came from the first military district.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You did not see, did you, any documents concerning the resubordination of your unit to the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall seeing any such document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now call up document P359. I believe it's a public document. If we could zoom in, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You discussed this document with the Prosecutor yesterday. I don't know if this is good enough for you to see. Maybe we could again zoom out so that you can see who sent this document to whom. Look at the bottom first and then the top part.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an interim report that Major-General Stanislav Galic is sending to the Main Staff of the VRS, the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To be precise, because you talked about this yesterday, when you say "Commander Stanislav Galic," he is commander of what?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander, Major-General Stanislav Galic, was commander of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As we can see, this is an interim report. The first sentence reads: "On 27 December 1993, under the plan of Operation Pancir-2 an attack has been planned by the Combat Group 1 under the command of Colonel Stupar, Commander of the 72nd Special Brigade..." and so on. When I read this document, can we see that the Combat Group 1 commanded by Colonel Stupar was part of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps in these combat operations?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can the Chamber please move into private session. 3 [Private session] [Confidentiality lifted by order of Trial Chamber I]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to call up document P353, which is the war diary of the Guards Brigade, page, in English, 5, and page, in English, 7 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it 5 or 7 in English?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the entry for the 5th of January at 1800 hours. If you could scroll the B/C/S version down a bit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this entry that you entered, this is your signature, isn't it, Mr. Tesic? It states: "Pursuant to the order of the Commander of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, part of the Command -- exits and takes possession of the forward command post at Donja Josanica village from the 6th of January to the 8th of January, 1994." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is my handwriting, and what you read out is exactly as it reads, and the commander of the unit issued those orders; I just wrote them down.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, but you agree with me that the commander of the unit received those orders from the commander of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I ask something that needs clarification for me here. I note that entry number 13, the one that we are reading, is entered on the 5th of January, 1994, at 1800 hours, and a subsequent one is entered an hour earlier. Entry number 14. Can that -- are you able to explain that, Mr. Tesic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the next page in B/C/S could be shown to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is entered at 1700 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, 1700 hours. That is an hour earlier than 1800 hours.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. 1700 hours is an hour earlier than 1800 hours, but the one that is entered earlier came after the one that is entered later. Are you able to explain that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since this goes for a corps commander's order, most probably when the document was received, the operations officer, Mr. Paunovic entered the elements from that order into this logbook; it must have been received around 5.00, and then later on elements were registered that I didn't enter. Most probably, the order from the commander came in the written form, and Paunovic referred to it and specified that it reached the commander at 1700 hours when he was entering it into this book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I do not want to pretend to understand that explanation. I just don't understand what you are saying.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you'll allow me to expound on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is possible that this document went through other books, maybe must have been in the general affairs office that it was entered into the logbook.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says corps commander's order, pursuant to the needs and the approval of the Chief of the General Staff of the Yugoslavia army, the 2nd Special Brigade shall leave. It was done concurrently. The warrant officer who maintains the logbook did his part of the job, entered this there. I registered and recorded activities which took part at 6.00 p.m.. In the meantime, that order must have reached Paunovic, and he recorded it as at the 1700 hours when was the moment when this order came through the general affairs office and came to the logbook, into the logbook. This is a separate document apart from the war diary. We can look it up in the logbook. I don't remember how it is recorded there. But also, it could be a clerical error in recording the exact time. It's also a possibility. I shouldn't state something I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, that last explanation is better. The first one I still don't understand. What is the time that is mentioned in this column? Location, date, and time. Time for what? Isn't it time for entering something in the logbook?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. When that order arrived, it should state the time and date of the entry of the content. I agree with you. But I wouldn't wish to speculate or provide any further comment on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You just don't provide any further comment. Because I mean, if this is not the time of entry of this point, this entry here, then this date and time means nothing. It can only explain what is taking place on this document. We can't explain this through another document that is not here, can we?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you are right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could keep this B/C/S page, entry 15, and if you could scroll down the English, B/C/S version. We are still sticking to this issue on who the orders on combat activities is received from.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is entry dated 6th of January, 1994, and it says: Pursuant to the order of General Galic, Lieutenant-Colonel Stojimirovic will take over the command of the OG north, or operations group north, et cetera, et cetera. Do you agree with me that undoubtedly this entry reflects that the order concerning the structure of combat activities on the ground came from the commander of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps? Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This order referred to here did not come from General Panic; rather, it came from the commander of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, let's not speculate. Maybe he was cognizant of that as well. I agree.
