So on the basis of what I just showed you, do you agree with my thesis that in terms of your combat activities, your superior officers received their orders from the VRS command structure, in other words, from the commander of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of this, such a statement could be deducted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us remain in private session dealing with this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The next page I would like to discuss is the blank entry under the number 16. But still, while we're still on this page, Mr. Paunovic prepared those or entered those entries; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go to the next page in the B/C/S, please, and stick with the English page as it is. Let me be more precise. B/C/S, page 7, and English, page 8. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Here we can see a blank entry under the number 16, and under 17 we see that Paunovic entered this entry in column 4; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We don't have it in the English, that entry 17. You said they must keep this page. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I would like the following -- next page in the English version to be shown, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So entry 17, under column 4, you recognise the signature as being that of Mr. Paunovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's go to the next page in both B/C/S and English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Here in entry 18, you recognise Mr. Paunovic's signature, don't you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next page in the B/C/S, and keep the present English page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In entries 19 and 20, column 4, you can recognise Mr. Paunovic's signature, don't you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next page in the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I believe entry 22, 21, 22, and 23, column 4 contains Paunovic's signature again?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then if we could scroll the B/C/S version down, we come again to your signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So we can see here, dated 15th of January, 1994, after awhile we see your signature again; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That would be entry, but -- we see the date but don't see the number. So from what I saw before entry number 16, the last time you had entered entries into the war diary was the 5th of January, and then the next time you did so was on the 15th of January; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the meantime, your colleague Radoje Paunovic did the job. My question to you is, did anybody tell you that something ought not to be entered into the war diary? Can you remember that?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody told me that something ought not be entered into the war diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did your colleague Paunovic tell you that somebody else had told him that something ought not be entered into the war diary?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't tell me that somebody had told him not to enter something into the war diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you -- after the 7- or 10-day break, next time around when you did enter something into the war diary on the 15th January, 1994, you had no reason to check the preceding pages and the preceding entries; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you do not know -- you don't know that the entry 16, which is blank, was not blank at that time as well?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer you this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. While we are still in private session, now I'm going to ask you, since I presume you had occasion to go through this war diary in a detailed manner, what I see from the war diary and other documents is as follows: It's very often that they make mention of planning of combat operations, but I never see any entry explaining that a combat action had been executed. Isn't it true that you, as you said, did not move a single metre forward while you were there at Vogosca out in the field?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree with you. Actions were planned, but nothing was being carried out on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We may go back to open session, Your Honours, briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your examination-in-chief, you testified and you confirmed that today -- that two days before departure on the 30th December, 1993 - 1993, you are correct - that you had received from your superior officer the tasks to go to that mission; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you did your proofing with the Prosecution, we received proofing notes which reflects that you stated to them that you do not know anybody refusing to go on this mission among your officers, fellow officers and troops; at least, this is what we are led to believe from the proofing notes.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In respect of the first group, which departed in mid-December, where part of your unit also departed, do you know -- do you have any information whether they volunteered to go on that mission or not?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not have such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Another question and then we will have to go back into private session. You stated to the Prosecution during your proofing before your testimony that during that mission you wore VJ uniforms, you remember saying so.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You did not remove the insignia of the Army of Yugoslavia at that time?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not mention insignia. No question was asked. I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You do not recall taking them off?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I do not recall taking them off.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, we have to go back into private session again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can the Chamber please move into private session. 16 [Private session] [Confidentiality lifted by order of Trial Chamber I]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Earlier today in response to a question from the Prosecution when you were shown entries in the war diary, you confirmed that certain officers from your unit did train VRS soldiers to use sniper rifles, and we can see that from the entries.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now call up, please, another entry in the war diary, P353, page 15 in B/C/S and page 16 in English, an entry for 2000 hours on the 18th of January, 1994. Just a moment. I find the hard copy easier.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I am reading the second sentence here: "A sabotage group 30 men strong attacked our positions above Srednje early in the morning. The attack was repelled where the men were awake. However, at the points where the men were still asleep, the Turks slaughtered eight of our men, wounded others, and captured a PAM, an anti-aircraft machine gun, as well as a mortar." Paunovic made this entry, but do you remember these events?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've heard of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's when these men of the Army of Republika Srpska, I suppose, not your men, got killed?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of the Army of Republika Srpska got killed. I don't know to which brigade they belonged, but it was an area near Orlovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember during your stay there, was it a standing warning to you that sabotage groups of the enemy could make incursions and also use their own snipers against you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that the main point of training snipers is to counter the sabotage terrorist groups of the enemy?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Between your positions near Vogosca - and we'll show the map later - between Vogosca and the city of Sarajevo, there were BH Army positions, correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In view of that frontline, you had no opportunity of ever seeing the city of Sarajevo, correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From our positions, Sarajevo could not be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you hear at that time that VRS snipers were shooting at civilians in Sarajevo? Did any such information reach you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now move back into open session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Hopefully, we'll now have a very clear picture of where exactly you were, and I'll ask you to mark certain positions on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like a copy of the 65 ter map 9244 to be placed in front of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now, we'll see, Mr. Tesic, if this map will be of assistance to all of us in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now zoom in some more. Zoom out now, please, once. Now we need to zoom in some more and raise the name of "Vogosca" a bit higher up, and now move it a bit to the left. Perfect.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, does this map look good to you? I'll ask you to mark certain positions.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, I'd like you to take the electronic pen and mark certain things on the screen. The first question: At which location did you arrive exactly on the 31st of December when you came to the area of Vogosca? Where were you, if you can find it? And put a number 1 there. Larger.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I showed the facility approximately, but my pen moved to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You wanted to show Hotel Park?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we erase it and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We can do it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So it's the location of Hotel Park, and now put a number 1 there.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in the documents we reviewed certain locations I mentioned. First of all, you said that one of the places you were close to at one point was the Golf VW factory.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're talking about the factory -- the automobile factory Sarajevo TAS. Shall I put a circle around it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you're able to. Put number 2 there.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On this map, are you able to mark approximately the positions that your units held without moving an inch, as you said? On which positions were they?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can mark it roughly because they were together with the Vogosca Brigade, but I'll mark the positions. Part of the 2nd Motorised Battalion, I'll mark it with 3, and part of our police, number 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You mean military police?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. Mr. Lukic, that statement, part of the 2nd Motorised -- well, that was not your question. Okay. It's changed now. Thank you. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Anything else you remember?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In these gaps we had three tanks, but they were static. I'm not quite sure that I can mark the approximate position of one tank, which is here. One was close to the 2nd Motorised Battalion. I'm not sure about the third. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Put a T near these two dots.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you see on this map the name of Zuc hill or elevation and put a circle around it?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Lower down there is the same name, Zuc. I don't understand if this is a village.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is a trig point.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Put number 5 there.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This place marked 5, Zuc, this was a position held by the BH Army, correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I heard. It was not one of our controlled areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Positions 3 and 4, was that the forward combat line, or were some units ahead of you?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 200 metres ahead of us, there were trenches of the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You mean the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you draw an imaginary line, perhaps change the colour and use blue. Can we use the blue pen?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of their positions were here in the area of Ugorsko, and we could not observe any further ahead because of the lay of the land.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we erase the 5 near Zuc and redraw it in blue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you erase it, you are going to erase everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. I suppose it's clear that number 5, Zuc, was also an area controlled by the BH Army. It's not in dispute.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct. THE COURT: The only point, Mr. Lukic, is that you referred the witness to another Zuc below the one Zuc. Now, I don't know which one is the correct Zuc that was the -- that was held by the BH Army. There's a bigger Zuc down below there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Right. You see, Mr. Tesic, there are two markings Zuc, one in smaller letters, one in larger letters. Is this a distinction between a place and a hill?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were holding Zuc hill and Orlic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is Orlic also a hill?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Trig point 876. A very dominant elevation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This Orlic, can you also mark that hill and put number 6 there?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, to be very precise, can you put a blue circle on top of the red on position 5? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this map, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The map is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D18, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And to have a complete picture, I'd like to call up another map. 3D 1D00-1821. Sorry, I'll repeat this. 1D00-1821. 3D. I think we could zoom in a bit. A bit more. Perfect.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, if you can find your way around this map, I'll only ask you where Vogosca and Zuc and your positions were. Can you mark that?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we zoom in a bit more. Scroll up, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, perhaps, can you recognise Vogosca?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't venture a guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps during the break I can prepare a hard copy. Your Honours, could we take the break now, because I would like to ask one more question on this map after the break and then proceed with my final questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Very well then. We'll take a break and come back at half past 12.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If one copy, one hard copy could be given to the Prosecution and to the witness. We were quite ambitious, but nevertheless, I'm a bit skeptical about the success of our venture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are we able to see it on the monitor?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, if this means anything to you, what I'm interested in is for you to find the Vogosca and the Zuc on this map, the Zuc hill, to explain those two matters here. If you can't locate them, then I'll try a third tack.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So could we please recall 65 ter 2942 map, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, please take a look. What I'd like you to do is to try to locate Vogosca and the Zuc elevation on this map. Would you like it to be zoomed up?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no need for that. Thank you. This is an aerial photography, and as an officer, I know how to read those maps or photos. I can see here the Sarajevo airport, and I presume, I dare not state for certain, but here where you see the sides of the world, this in the upper left corner should be the area of Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you could encircle it.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't be certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then, I will give it up, because I don't want to lead you into any speculations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like us to go back into private session, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session. 16 [Private session] [Confidentiality lifted by order of Trial Chamber I]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we call up Exhibit P356 on the screen, please. Could we please focus on the title or the heading of this document, please, on the top of the page. In the B/C/S, please. Move it to the left, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In answering questions concerning this document yesterday, on page 1921/4 of the transcript, you stated that this was an order. Could you please take a look at this copy and tell us whether something different is written here. I don't want to lead you or suggest an answer to you.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot interpret this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Should I then put it to you that the word here is "briefing"?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appears to be so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the same in the English translation, so I wanted to avoid any confusion, so we have confirmed that this is a briefing report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please zoom out the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This document does not show to whom it was addressed; at least, I could not find any reference.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What you testified about this was as follows: In the first paragraph, there is a list of the units that entered, and I'll read it out: Parts of the Guards Brigade was used to re-enforce the 72nd Special Brigade and enter the formation of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps on the 17th December, 1993. Upon the arrival of the Guards Motorised Brigade on the 31st December, 1993, to Vogosca the reinforcement units left the formation of the 72nd Special Brigade and entered the formation of the Guards Motorised Brigade. The current numerical strength of the Guards Motorised Brigade is 210 men, officers --

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Civilians and contract soldiers, I presume?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can't find your bearings with all those acronyms. So what I'm interested in, since I'm starting with my closing questions, all the troops, all the men that were engaged from the Guards Brigade over there, from this document it is visible that on the 13th of January, 1994, from your unit there are a total of 210 men from the first group and the group that subsequently arrived. Is this the maximum number of men from your unit that were there, give or take a few? So is this the total of Guards Motorised Brigade members who were there at that time?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the overall number of men there, give or take five or ten men.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In relation to the overall number of the peacetime composition of the Guards Brigade - we know that in wartime the number goes up - this number, this figure is tantamount to approximately 10 percent of the men of the Guards Brigade who were actually there?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given that overall number, the overall strength was around 1500 men, then you could easily calculate what this number was in percentage terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the next paragraph, there is mention of the units. You testified about that, but what I'd like to hear more about is the tank platoon M-84. How many tanks are usually there in a platoon?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So this is what you showed us. So you had a total of three tanks with you there at that time?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will read out paragraph 4. It says: "Problems. Strong anti-armoured --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. Can we just scroll to paragraph 4, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "Strong anti-armoured resistance of the enemy and insufficient number of our forces for tracking attacks launched by tanks and the armoured personnel carriers can inflict serious losses to our forces. Tanks have only .5 combat munition sets without any serious prospects to improve the resupply of the munition in the next day." This is what the report says.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So could we conclude from paragraph 4 that the enemy held very strong positions and could inflict substantial losses on you if you were to go on an attack; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the thinking of the Commander of the Guards Brigade, Lieutenant-Colonel Ljubisa Stojimirovic, the man who signed this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was mentioned yesterday in one of the documents that there was a possibility that, after your departure, members of the 67th - correction, 63rd Parachute Brigade from Nis would take your positions. Do you have any information that somebody went to replace you after you departed in January 1994?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not have such information, but I don't think that anybody else went over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My position, Mr. Tesic, is that in the Pancir operation, which was an attack operation of the VRS, that in it the Vogosca Brigade, the Rajlovac Brigade and one brigade of the Krajina Corps, one brigade of the Herzegovina corps and 500 members of the police of the Republic of Srpska took part in it. Do you agree with me that those units represented a substantial force of an army in an operation in such an area?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you listed are respectable forces for a commander. I would also want to note that that area, we had Kosevo Brigade as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And from the VJ, from the Army of Yugoslavia, who was present there in accordance with my thesis and my information in the first group that was led by Colonel Stupar, there were 120 men, and then there was the other group which came with your unit, so to bring the total slightly above 200 men who were engaged in that action; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your statement to the Prosecution, you said -- and we can bring it up on the screen if necessary, you said that at paragraph 81, you stated there, to be as precise as possible: "Due to loss of eight officers, 72nd Brigade was in a poor state." Do you recall saying -- describing the situation as such when you came to that place?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These were the words of the superior officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you confirmed to me during the first part of my cross-examination that the Guards Brigade really had a status of an elite military unit; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I presume that the 72nd Special Brigade also did bear such an epithet of an elite unit?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not a commander so that I could assess this, but I presume yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that from the 15th of December until your pullout towards the end of January, you and your units and the units preceding you there did not help in any substantial way to that offensive action since you were holding positions without advancing throughout that period?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The units of the Guards Brigade did not participate in offensive actions during their stay from the 31st December, 1993, through 30th of January, 1994, when we were already back in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While you were there, the units of the Army of Republika Srpska did not capture Zuc hill?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard of no such thing, and I would have heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Tesic. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before you sit down, Mr. Lukic, could we bring that exhibit, please, on the screen, P356. Mr. Tesic, can you explain something for me here which is not quite clear. It says: "The elements of the Guards Motorised Brigade units reinforced the 72nd Special Brigade, thus entering the formation of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps on the 17th December, 1993. Upon the arrival of the Guards Motorised Brigade in Vogosca on the 31st December, 1993, the reinforcement units left the formation of the 72nd Special Brigade and entered the formation of the Guards Motorised Brigade." And that's where my question is. Now, these are the Guards Motorised Brigade units who are leaving the 72nd Special Brigade and entering the formation of the Guards Motorised Brigade. Were there two Guards Motorised Brigades?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there was only one Motorised Guards Brigade. In this passage, reference is made to a part of a unit of the 2nd Motorised Battalion equivalent to 60 to 80 members who reinforced the 72nd Special Brigade. With the arrival of the Guards Brigade in the 31st of December, 1993, they leave the 72nd Special Brigade and join the Guards Brigade that had arrived in Vogosca in the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And these Guards Brigades that had arrived are also from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Like the ones who are joining them? Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And when we talk of the current numerical strength being 210 men, is that the current numerical strength of the two parts of the Guards Motorised Brigade put together, or is it just the one part?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's just one part of the unit, and I said the same to the Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure. Now, if you put the two parts together, what would have been the strength of the Guards Motorised Brigade? Numerical strength?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are talking about two parts. If we take one part only, the number, the total number is 210.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And if we take two parts, what is the number, sir? That's the question. I don't know whether the two parts were equal halves or 80 percent and 20 percent. So when we put the two parts together, what was the numerical strength?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the first part is 60 to 80 men. The second part is 210 to 220 men that arrive from Belgrade. The total --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Around 300, give or take?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- is around 210.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter must have made a mistake. Can the witness repeat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please repeat yourself. The interpreter didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The total number of the Guards Brigade on the 31st December, 1993, was around 210 men.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The second part was 110 to 120.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So it's something like 320 to 330, the total sum? I must be missing something.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can I try to assist. The Prosecution and I both looked at documents and have a clear picture, so we can just ask the witness to confirm what we understand. In mid-December, one part of the Guards Brigade left, as the witness says, 60 to 80 men. Then on the 31st December, another part of their brigade arrived, around ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 120 to 130 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, the first group left the 72nd Special Brigade who left for Belgrade and joined the second group so that together they totalled 210. I think that's what the witness meant to say.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That clears me. Thank you very much. You said you are done with your cross-examination. Madam Sutherland, any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me just say that we were in private session until the end of my cross-examination. I don't know if the Prosecutor wishes to stay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Lukic. I stayed in private session because I wanted clarification of this document. May the document please be removed from the screen. Thank you very much. May we please move into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Madam Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, in cross-examination this morning, you were taken to your statement and asked about officers who were part of the 30th Personnel Centre who became officers of the VRS, and you said that that was based on what you had heard from the officers who through the services of the 30th Personnel Centre became officers of the VRS. Who did you speak to, which officers, the names of the officers that you spoke to?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first officer that comes to mind is my deputy commander of the battalion from Vukovar, Slavko Stijekovic [phoen]. He left the Guards Brigade to go to Republika Srpska, and he was assigned to some duties in the area of Banja Luka. There were other commanding officers who went to Republika Srpska from other units of the Guards Brigade. I know some left from the military police battalion, some lieutenants who names I don't remember. One lieutenant went to Bijeljina from the 2nd Motorised Battalion under Commander Borovcanin. I later saw that man and talked to him. I can't remember if he was battalion commander or company commander. I spoke to more than four people, and they all said they went there voluntarily and their orders came from their superiors.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour and Defence. I should have given you the page number, 32, of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And that was in relation to sending people who were born in BiH?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those who were born in Bosnia-Herzegovina were sent there after an interview in the personnel administration of the General Staff and after a decision was written on their assignment to the VRS. I cannot tell you what exactly that procedure involved.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You said that their orders came from their superior. What orders are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are talking about orders from their superior officers. The battalion commander would convey orders from brigade commander. We are talking down to brigade level, and I believe the same apply to the Special Units Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: One moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, you said that orders came from their superior officers. What was the nature of the orders?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Officers who were born in Republika Srpska were invited to a meeting, and what happened then, I wouldn't know, but all I know, that some of them told me later that they were going to Republika Srpska to assume new duties. I didn't attend that meeting, and I can't tell you anything further about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I want to turn to another topic now. Pages 34 and 35 of today's transcript, you were asked a question by the Defence. A proposition was put to you that when your unit went to Vogosca, you didn't participate in active much -- you didn't participate much in active action, you were mainly holding the line, to which you replied that did you not move an inch during your entire stay there.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I told you, too, during proofing, save for an intervention carried out with a couple of vehicles and a group of 20 members or so of the military police in the area of Srednje, and that was reflected in one of the documents shown today.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The VJ was working in tandem with the VRS, wasn't it? Or were you working in tandem with the VRS, I should better say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think this is leading, the way the question is formulated. I'm not sure the Prosecution should be allowed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I reformulated it to say, were you working in tandem? The answer is yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That term "tandem" is inadmissible in military terminology. The relationship, superior/subordinate, is always dominant. That's the only thing that's in issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I will rephrase my question. Were you coordinating operations with the VRS units?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't answer that question because that was exclusively within the jurisdiction of the unit commander. Operations officers are not involved in those activities. As for the drafting of maps and documents, the operations officer receives all instructions from the commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, may we go into closed session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into closed session. 21 [Closed session] [Confidentiality lifted by order of Trial Chamber I]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in closed session.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could we have Exhibit P353, the war diary on the screen, please. If we could go to page 10 of the English. It's entry number 18 of the 10th of January, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, you can see there a reference to the evening of the 11th of January: An officer from the platoon shall go to the Rajlovac Brigade Commander Major Radic to agree about next activities." Is this coordinating with the VRS?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is about the military police platoon for special purposes, a very small unit, and very few members of it were present in that area, so we cannot really talk about an operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could we go to the next entry, number 19, entry number 19 on the 11th of January, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: We can see there that the commander of the Military Police Special Purposes Platoon shall send senior sergeant - and it's a last name illegible in the English translation - to the Rajlovac Brigade Commander Major Radic for the reconnaissance of the direction of the engagement of the snipers. Is this coordinating with the VRS?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is probably about an agreement, an understanding that had been reached, but I couldn't tell you what exactly because I never went to the area of Rajlovac in the period covered by the war diary.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could go to page 13 I think of the English translation. It's around entry 26. It's just below that. It's the 17th of January, 1994, at 630 hours. If we could go a couple of pages on to page 13, and it's the bottom entry.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, we see here under tasks: "Sergeant 1st Class Veljko Sironja from the tank platoon shall carry out reconnaissance of certain directions for the next activities with the Rajlovac Brigade commander." Is that coordination with the VRS?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The assignments issued here were planned before for this period, but they were not actually implemented in the field.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: We can also see below there, point 3: "Two groups of snipers shall remain with brigades until the 19th of January, 1994." Which brigades were they, VRS brigades?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. I did write this, although I can't remember it. That's probably right. I think there was a document saying they were supposed to stay there from the 17th through the 19th, the one where there was a reference to snipers and training. You can look up that document again, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Would you say this is coordination with the VRS?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I noted this, and as for expressing an opinion, it was up to the commander Lieutenant-Colonel Stojimirovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page, please, page 14 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: We can see halfway down the page, now, this is for an entry of the 17th of January, 1994, at 2000 hours, and it's around -- it's just after -- so it's on page 14 of the English translation. And we see towards the bottom half of the page -- I'll wait for the B/C/S. Do you see where it says "orders for the 18th of January, 1994"? "With one combat group from the Military Police Special Purpose Platoon and a military police battalion detachment, in cooperation with the forces of the Vogoscanska Brigade launch an attack along the axis K870-K850; in cooperation with combat group 2 along the axis Perivoj-Vis and facilitate the attack of the BG2." Do you see that entry? Do you see this is as cooperation with the VRS? Coordination, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you've read is correct, but I see you are mentioning a detachment, but it's not actually a detachment. It's a group from the military police platoon for special purposes. It's the equivalent of eight men and a squad from the military police platoon. A squad is up to eight men. So it was a maximum of 16 men that engaged in coordinated action with, I don't see any more on my page, what kind of coordinated action it was, I don't know, but it was a small number of members of the Guards Brigade the way it's written here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we can go to entry number 34, which is on page 20 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And then we see the reference halfway down the page to: "All are required maximum vigilance and to be ready to be engaged in active defence."

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what is written here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And then down further below under "Orders," number 2: "Send a Praga" - it says in the English translation - "from Lieutenant-Colonel Josipovic within the formation of the BG-2 in accordance with the previously received tasks on the 23rd of January, 1994..." You said that Colonel Josipovic was in the VRS? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And who is BG-2?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't answer that question. So much time has elapsed, I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We have seen on previous entries BG group being interpreted as combat group 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I was wanting the witness to clarify, was BG-2 part of the VRS or part of the VJ troops?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then put the question that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, was BG -- do you know whether BG-2, i.e., the combat group, was part of the VRS or the VJ troops?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can here only express my opinion on the basis of what is written here. Combat group 2 is within the composition of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And it says at -- under order number 1: "At 2000 hours, Major Cvjetinovic was ordered to strengthen the Ilijas Brigade in the sector of Srednje to resubordinate one BOV." Is that an armoured personal carrier?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a combat armoured vehicle with a 20-millimetre weapon, a wheeled vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: "To resubordinate that vehicle to Semizovac garrison for the commander of the Ilijas Brigade Captain Savic by 1000 hours on the 23rd of January, 1994." Now --

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Who does the Ilijas Brigade belong to?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ilijas Brigade is one of the units of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you see this entry as coordinating operations with the VRS?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a matter for the commanders to decide, maybe help in personnel and materiel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: To which army did Major Cvjetinovic belong?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Major Cvjetinovic was a member of the Guards Brigade of the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If we could go to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But he was born in the wider area of Srebrenica, Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we move away from this page, I just have a question to ask. That entry number 2 under "Orders" which says: "Send a Praga from Lieutenant-Colonel Josipovic within the formation of the BG-2 in accordance with the previously received tasks on the 23rd of January, 1994, at 630 hours." So the tasks were received on the 23rd of January. 1994; is that how it reads?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't see the whole document, but the page shown to me does not show that. I can read out item 2 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 22nd of January, 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we show that, please, because -- yes. I think it's at the bottom of the page in the B/C/S. Could we please scroll up or turn the next page. Is that right, that the tasks were received on the 23rd of January, 1994?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Probably, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, but what's written there? Can you tell us what's written there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm reading the second part: Composition of the combat group 2 to Guards Brigade element commander is to enter the battle group composition who will command the mortar platoon for the next two or three days. This document requires for a commanding officer to be sent to command a small unit of two or three mortars for the next two or three days within the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could go back to the previous page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, I'm going to ask that we go back to the previous page, please, in the B/C/S. Right. Now, let us confirm one thing. This entry number 34, sir, can you tell us whose signature is that? Who entered this entry? Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is my handwriting, and this is my signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Right. Now, you tell us -- can we scroll down, please, to the bottom of that page. Right. Can you read that entry number 2, which starts with: "Send a Praga from Lieutenant-Colonel Josipovic..." and read it up to where it says "... 23rd January, 1994 ..." I would like you to tell me -- you to read your own handwriting and tell us what it is you wrote there.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness read slower, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please read slow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm reading. On the day 23rd of January, 1994, at 0630, to the composition of combat group 2, one Praga is to be sent in accordance with a previously received task by Lieutenant-Colonel Josipovic. And from 630 to the composition of combat group 2, one officer is to enter coming from the 2nd Motorised Battalion who is to command a platoon of 60-millimetre mortar to command over them for the next two or three days. Your Honours, in the first part of this item, we are discussing sending one Praga to the combat -- composition of combat group 2 of probably VRS. At the same time, on the next day, on the 23rd January, one commanding officer from the 2nd Motorised Battalion of the Guards Brigade of Army of Yugoslavia from Belgrade is sent to command a platoon of 60-millimetre mortars for the subsequent two or three days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So -- and this was issued on the 22nd of January in the evening hours during the briefing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Tesic, because --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much for understanding me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, can I finish, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You have cleared an issue which was causing me serious problems, because what you are telling us is something that is to happen in the future. What is written here is something that has happened in the past, and my question was, how did it happen on the 23rd if the entry was on the 21st? You see, I must complain, therefore, about the translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You know, this translation here says that "in accordance with previously received tasks" on the --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I think the word "on" should be "for."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Beg your pardon? It says: "In accordance with previously received tasks on the 23rd of January..."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, I think the word "for" -- the word "on" 23rd January, it should be "for." In accordance with the previously received tasks for the 23rd of January, which is just the witness has just explained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's true. That's true, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, I agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But I'm saying check your translations.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Your translations are very bad, or otherwise, I don't understand the language.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And also, at the beginning of paragraph 2, Your Honour, "Send a Praga from..." As the witness has just explained, it's to send a Praga to Lieutenant-Colonel Josipovic. That's the way I understood the witness, so we will have this document revised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is this a CLSS translation?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then I think this document must be MFI'd, notwithstanding the fact that the Defence has not objected because it is not telling us the story that is being told by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, this is supposed to be P353. If it is not already MFI'd, may it please be marked for identification, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That will be Exhibit P353 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, I'm done, Judge. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, in the document we are exhibited now, there is a concept that has been repeated many times and is the one related to active defence. Here in the document it says: All are required maximum vigilance and to be ready to engage in active defence. In this concept, I would like to put it in relation to what you have said on the transcripts on the 24th November in page 5, lines 23 to 25. You said in relation to the question why your unit went to Vogosca, you said: "The reason why we were supposed to go there was to help pull out the 72nd Special Brigade from that area, to take over the bodies of aided members of that brigade, and to the extent possible to stabilize the part of the defence line held by the troops by the Vogosca Brigade of the VRS." The concept of stabilize into -- in connection with active defence, what are the hypotheses of action that the tactics require at that moment are indicated according to the situation? What is the meaning of stabilize within the concept of active defence? Could you give me an example of the hypotheses that could encounter a unit to make operational the concept of active defence with the tactical purpose of stabilize a line of defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One important thing is diminished: Combat moral of a unit. So a unit is ready to leave and withdraw the whole position, and the frontline saying, I don't want to be killed, I don't want to be here anymore, I'm going somewhere. Our coming there changed the awareness of those people and made them think, If those guys are coming here, why shouldn't I stick around? Am I being clear? When combat morale is diminished, it is very difficult to bring things into a prior state, and combat morale must have been diminished by the losses of the Vogosca Brigade of the VRS and the 72nd Special Brigade where seven officers and contract soldiers from within the VJ were killed in action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Are you saying, Mr. Tesic, that the concept of active defence involves only psychological support and strengthening morale or involves military action in relation to objectives that may bring the enemy toward you in order to advance their line of separation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that this does not go for of achieving dominant position in combat activities at a certain point and to prepare conditions for further assault. It was, rather, a situation held on to what you already have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, again, among the hypotheses for action, if you are given instructions to stabilize a line, and you find resistance, military active resistance, what do you do? You said you didn't move an inch. Didn't you move an inch because there were no need to defend the line because of the situation were already stabilized or you will have moved a kilometre if possible in order to establish a line, and were that were senior orders? I ask many questions to you, so please answer those that you consider more proper.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm glad that you are thinking along those lines. I'm trying to give you a proper valid answer. At no moment were we told that we should be ready to attack a facility so that to switch from defence into attack. We did not see such documents, neither could we discuss them. The basic task was to hold on to the area already controlled. If you noticed in the war diary, the first time when the commander of the Guards Brigade issues tasks and orders to his subordinated units, he says to perform active defence and, in the area from which active defence is being carried out, certain targets may be destroyed - military targets, I'm discussing here - that may appear in front of the area being defended within the area of responsibility of a particular unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: And the destruction of military objectives when necessary because of the challenges put to your line are also authorised within the mandate of a stabilisation of a line. Is that correct? Would you be inactive receiving this orders to stabilize a line facing a military action on the other part? You said destroy. Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, depending on what targets there are. Destroy a vehicle, a tank; or incapacitate, you can incapacitate a person; maybe neutralise, if we talk about a piece of weaponry. I just give you one example. A target must be either neutralised or destroyed or incapacitated so that the person defending the line should avoid a situation where it would be threatened or jeopardized or to avoid a unit being jeopardized if we are discussing a military unit or a military formation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: The concept of active defence involves also engagement. Engage, you said in one of your replies, engage the enemy, so active Defence is really one of the postures facing both potential combat, one of the tactics facing potential combat, military opposition, military attacks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One could think and talk in that manner, roughly, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: So that the strategic objectives given in one order are not strategic objectives in abstract, but they are subjected to the tactical practical situations of the day, of the hour, and of the minute; is that correct? Because a strategic objectives are in general, the outline of many tactics facing the reality of your actions, in military terms; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, first, a strategic goal is not issued to a brigade or battalion-level unit. Whether there was a strategic goal given to the units of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, I couldn't provide you with this information. I presume it existed, but I mustn't state it as certain because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I was just interested in how you understood the orders of active defence, engagement and stabilization among the potential situations that you may encounter facing in Vogosca the reality of a possible or potential army confrontation, and also to understand what you said, "I did not move an inch." Thank you very much, Mr. Tesic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Sutherland, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could turn to entry number 38 on page 23 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, this is an entry for the 26th of January, 1994, and it says: "The Guards Motorised Brigade commander carried out reconnaissance with the TG-1 Commander Lieutenant-Colonel Josipovic in the area of the Rajlovac and Ilidza Brigade for the purpose of further coordinated actions." Again, does this passage in the war diary show coordination between the VJ and the VRS, coordinating operations?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my handwriting and my signature, and I stated that the commander of the Guards Brigade at a certain -- was somewhere at a certain date. What they discussed, I don't know. I put down coordinated action. I was told to do so, and that's that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And who told you to do that?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I receive orders from my commander only, and most probably he said I was reconnaissing [as interpreted] in connection with further coordinated actions. And given that two days after this date indicated here we started our return to our Belgrade garrison in Serbia, most probably nothing ensued from all those joint reconnaissance trips, planned coordinated actions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And your superior officer, the Guards Motorised Brigade commander is Lieutenant-Colonel Stojimirovic?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, on page 34 of the transcript this morning, you were asked about your primary task of the unit -- sorry. A proposition was put to you whether you agreed that your primary task of the unit was to go to Vogosca and secure the location so that you could recover the bodies of the dead members of the 72nd Brigade, and you in your answer said: "I agree that our task was to recover the bodies of the members ever the 72nd Brigade." What did you do personally to recover the eight bodies?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally did not take part in retrieving those bodies. The Guards Brigade assigned certain officers from the intelligence security organs who, together with an officer from the 72nd Brigade, Major Radic, collected information and tried to get in contact with the other side, the BiH army, to affect the delivery of those bodies or an exchange of bodies so that we could recover the bodies of the members of the 72nd Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, what were you doing in Vogosca for the month of January 1994?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you explain? Do you mean me personally or my unit?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes. You said that the task was to recover the bodies of the members of the 72nd Brigade, and you have just explained that you didn't personally recover them. So what were you and your unit doing in January 1994?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Part of the officers of the Guards Brigade together with an officer from the 72nd Brigade who had stayed behind after the 72nd Brigade had left the composition of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps were active and involved on that case. The other members of the Guards Brigade together with the Vogosca Brigade carried out the defence of the area that they had control over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, I think that question was a very simple question. The question was, what were you and your unit doing in January 1994? Can you tell us what you did for the month of January 1994, you and your unit, in Vogosca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The unit carried out defence tasks together with the unit of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Does that answer your question, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I may follow that up tomorrow morning, Your Honour. I note the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Fair enough. We'll then take the break and -- adjourn for the day, rather, and come back tomorrow at 9.00 in the morning, same courtroom. And, Mr. Tesic, once again, you are warned not to discuss this case with anybody until you are excused from testifying. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 26th day of November, 2008, at 9.00 a.m. 23 24
